$description: Citation ledger for build-time evidence that lives OUTSIDE design-repo/ (sibling src/, CLONE_SPEC.md, config, reference/). verify_all.py checks every citation (range + quoted content) when the sibling source tree exists and WARNS (does not fail) when it is absent.
sourceRootConvention: Citations are path:line[-line] relative to the parent folder of design-repo/ (override with env DESIGN_REPO_SOURCE_ROOT).

router.value: none - a 54-line pushState router (no react-router dependency)

fonts.value: self-hosted woff2 in public/fonts (Chalet, Geist Pixel Square, Instrument Sans, Chivo Mono)

decisions.claim: Every word of page copy in the clone is ORIGINAL placeholder text written for the clone (not rig.ai's copy). All maxWords budgets and the example/fixtures derive from it; rig.ai wording is never pasted here (enforced by ORIGINAL_COPY_FINGERPRINT with hash-only fingerprints).
CSS custom properties on :root in src/index.css (oklch, verbatim from the original) are the token source of truth; tailwind.config.js points at them.
All breakpoints are max-width (desktop-first): xl <=1280, lg <=1024, tab 769-1024, md <=768, plus page-scoped 720/640/480/400.
10 inventory routes: 9 concrete paths + the /blog/<unknown-slug> not-found state of the post template. Any other path renders Home (no 404).

Homepage order: overlays, hero (embedded header + ticker), frame lines, spacer-top, problem, intro, offline, three-col, DOUBLE divider, how, capabilities, stats, terminal, early-access, faq, spacer-bottom, CTA (outside main), footer - with a rule divider between every pair of main sections.

All forms are front-end only: WaitlistForm fakes success after ~800ms; /waitlist persists an entry in localStorage ('rig-clone-waitlist'); the hardware survey saves locally. Turnstile, PostHog and the waitlist API were intentionally NOT recreated; an empty .turnstile-container keeps the 1rem margin.

Three WebGL canvases (intro #shader3, how #shader1, early-access #shader2) use src/lib/ditherShader.js, whose GLSL was written for the clone to approximate rig.ai's look (not ported, despite spec §15 saying 'port verbatim'). Two presets only: headline, how - modelled as a closed enum.

No scroll-reveal/fade-in anywhere. Real motion: ticker, watermark/pupil/btn glitches, eye tracking + blink, SMIL diagram, globe drift, stepper auto-advance + fill + card tween, terminal load-reveal + typing, FAQ grid-rows, CTA glitch + glow, blink dots, spinners; off-screen pausing via .is-visible.
Chamfer clip-path clips hover box-shadows and CTA glow; the ticker loop jumps (-50% of a viewport-wide flex row). Both are faithful, not bugs.

The only blog image (building-inference-engine) 502s at origin; the clone renders a neutral placeholder box with per-breakpoint aspect ratios -> asset role placeholder.blog-diagram (must-not-fabricate).

rig.ai is a live company. The clone ships its real wordmark/logo marks as build evidence; generated output must never reproduce them (asset roles brand.* must-not-fabricate), and Chalet London Nineteen Sixty is commercially licensed.

findings.claim: CLONE_SPEC §8 says the How card height tween uses easing [.25,.1,.25,1]. The original passes `easing` to the motion library, which ignores it and uses its easeOut default; the clone implements cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1), 400ms. Source wins; tokens/motion use cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1).

CLONE_SPEC §0.5/§16 says footer gets padding-inline 5% at <=1280. The clone source documents that this rule lives only in the original's blog-page stylesheet (measured 0px on the homepage) and does not apply it; the footer contract follows the source.

There is no prefers-reduced-motion rule anywhere in src/ (grep -ri reduce src matches only blog prose). Every non-'none' motion pattern therefore has reducedMotionHandledInSource=false; the const fallbacks in motion-patterns.json are requirements for generated pages (warn rule REDUCED_MOTION_UNHANDLED_IN_SOURCE), not observed behaviour.

ORIGINAL_COPY_FINGERPRINT found exactly one clone string that is verbatim original-site wording: the footer copyright/legal-name line in src/content.js. It is withheld from this repo (budget records only its word count; example/fixtures use a neutral 'Example Company' line). Recommend rewriting it in the clone.

The clone's placeholder copy still names the real company ('Introducing Rig', 'Rig AI Inc.' in legal.js, 'rig.ai' as link text). Flagged by warn rule SOURCE_BRAND_IN_COPY on every fixture; production generation must substitute the client's brand.

intro-diagram.svg and surveillance-eye.svg are extracted verbatim from the original markup and carry the original's short text labels (incl. the RIG name); Intro.jsx inlines the diagram without replacing them. Asset roles flag them; replace labels before production.
The spec's card-title strings for steps 2-3 (original-site labels, not reproduced here) differ from the clone's cardTitle values; the clone copy is authoritative per the copy rule.
Both legal docs open with an extra 'placeholder, not a real policy' notice block, so the clone has 108/22 top-level blocks vs the spec's 107/21 inventory. Budgets include it.

Clone copy lengths exceed some spec ranges: longest compressing-post paragraph 182 words (spec 3-126), inference title 10 words (spec 4-9). Budgets follow the clone copy (the copy rule), so these are the real maxWords.
Legal copy links a placeholder address on the reserved example.com domain via mailto:. Modelled as link kind 'email-placeholder' restricted to example.com/.org/.net - never a real inbox.

The only external links in the clone are the dashboard's X/LinkedIn share intents, built at runtime from the page's referral link; modelled as link kind 'share-intent' (network enum) so a PageSpec never carries a URL. Footer social links are '#' placeholders.

Two source comments are stale: visibility.js says it is called from App.jsx (it is called from Home.jsx and Waitlist.jsx); CONVENTIONS.md says dividers are rendered by App.jsx (they are in Home.jsx). Contracts cite the real call sites.

screenshotNote: Playwright screenshots and measurement scripts from the recon/QA sessions were consulted during the build but live outside the project in an ephemeral scratch area; they are not cited or shipped. CLONE_SPEC.md carries the measured values.
